improvements: Sun Jie feels more like a busy staff member and less like an authorial truth-delivery device.
Luo Cheng's status discomfort remains visible after removing several witty recovery lines.
The chapter trusts the office workflow and resume edits to show the gap between training and direct experience.
The printing-shop section is shorter and no longer explains the mismatch after the reader has already seen it.
The mundane ending survives subtraction and does not require a thematic closing image.
losses_that_are_acceptable: v2 contains less explicit explanation of why student-affairs labor changes Luo's view of the role.
v2 has fewer memorable lines and less conversational sparkle.
some readers may need to infer more about Luo's identity anxiety from context and later chapters.
remaining_risks: Sun Jie is still more verbally precise than many real busy staff members; later scenes should show her tired, mistaken, unavailable or less patient at times.
The full novel must not make every chapter hinge on a document, table, file version or checklist simply because these devices work well in this pilot.
Luo's warmer and more adaptive personality needs scenes away from institutional consultation so he does not become only the man who asks good career questions.
next_recommendation: Do not draft all remaining chapters. Draft the actual opening candidate next, then compare opening energy against this pilot. Keep each new full chapter disposable until it passes subtraction and anti-AI review.
